papers.title: Stability of solutions to stochastic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: We provide a general framework for the stability of solutions to stochastic partial differential equations with respect to perturbations of the drift. More precisely, we consider stochastic partial differential equations with drift given as the subdifferential of a convex function and prove continuous dependence of the solutions with regard to random Mosco convergence of the convex potentials. In particular, we identify the concept of stochastic variational inequalities (SVI) as a well-suited framework to study such stability properties. The generality of the developed framework is then laid out by deducing Trotter type and homogenization results for stochastic fast diffusion and stochastic singular p-Laplace equations. In addition, we provide an SVI treatment for stochastic nonlocal p-Laplace equations and prove their convergence to the respective local models.

papers.title: Regularity analysis for stochastic partial differential equations with nonlinear multiplicative trace class noise
papers.abstract: In this article spatial and temporal regularity of the solution process of a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) of evolutionary type with nonlinear multiplicative trace class noise is analyzed.

papers.title: Talagrand Concentration Inequalities for Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: One way to define the concentration of measure phenomenon is via Talagrand inequalities, also called transportation-information inequalities. That is, a comparison of the Wasserstein distance from the given measure to any other absolutely continuous measure with finite relative entropy. Such transportation-information inequalities were recently established for some stochastic differential equations. Here, we develop a similar theory for some stochastic partial differential equations.

It establishes frameworks for understanding the continuous dependence of solutions on perturbations, particularly through stochastic variational inequalities. Additionally, it addresses regularity issues in the presence of nonlinear multiplicative noise and examines the continuity of solutions in stochastic evolution equations.

proposal: This proposal aims to investigate the regularity and singularity propagation in stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), building on the foundational work of Gess and Tölle (2015) regarding stability under perturbations and Jentzen and Roeckner (2010) on regularity with nonlinear multiplicative noise. The gap identified is the lack of a comprehensive framework that integrates stability, regularity, and singularity propagation in SPDEs, particularly under varying noise conditions. The objective is to develop a unified approach that characterizes how singularities in the initial conditions or coefficients influence the regularity of solutions over time. Methodologically, we will employ advanced techniques from stochastic analysis, including Malliavin calculus and concentration inequalities as discussed by Khoshnevisan and Sarantsev (2017). The expected contribution includes establishing new results on the interplay between regularity and singularity in SPDEs, thus extending the existing literature by providing a more holistic view of solution behavior under stochastic influences. This work will differ from previous studies by focusing on the dynamic evolution of singularities in the context of stochastic perturbations, which has not been thoroughly addressed in the current literature.
